summary: The Highland Crown: nine highland states at the end of the Lake Road, ruled through a moot of clan chiefs, friendly to Furvior and free of the Treaty.

clan_moot.name: The Clan Moot
clan_moot.desc: The chiefs gather on the long green below the king's hall and speak in turn, the youngest first. A matter is settled when the last chief has nodded, which can take a week.

kings_word.name: The King's Word
kings_word.desc: Ocellio's word is carried by horn from valley to valley and obeyed before the echo fades. The chiefs murmur, and then they comply.

lake_tolls.name: Tolls of the Lake Road
lake_tolls.desc: Ostoroth keeps a toll-house at every ford of the Lake Road, and the price is carved on the lintel. Furvior's riders pay it with a smile and Postondoroth's wagons with a sigh.

passes_held.name: The Passes Held
passes_held.desc: Every pass of the high country has a hill-fort, a signal horn and a stock of boulders. If the Lake Road must be shut, it can be shut in a morning.

high_pastures.name: The High Pastures
high_pastures.desc: Sheep, goats and rough ponies graze the upland meadows from thaw to first frost, and the herd-books are kept in the king's hall. A kingdom of grass is rarely hungry.

letter_from_the_highlands.title: A Letter From the Highlands
letter_from_the_highlands.desc: A rider from Ostoroth arrives at the lake wharves with a letter sealed in blue wax. King Ocellio proposes that the lake and the highlands keep the Lake Road free together, and that neither will raise a hand against the other.

focuses.name: The Highland Crown
focuses.desc: Nine highland states answer to King Ocellio, who keeps his crown in a stone chest and wears it twice a year. The rest of the time he rides among his clans.

focuses.name: Ocellio's Court
focuses.desc: The king's hall stands on a hill above the capital, with a hearth the length of a ship. Hill-chiefs, drovers and envoys eat at the same long tables.

focuses.name: The Highland Clans
focuses.desc: Each clan keeps its own banner and its own feud. The king calls them to his side with horn-calls and cattle, and most of them answer.

focuses.name: The Clan Moot
focuses.desc: The chiefs meet in open air on the long green and agree the year's law. The king sits among them, and has one voice like any other.

focuses.name: The King's Word
focuses.desc: Ocellio sends sealed commands down the valleys by horn and runner, and the chiefs find themselves answering to one man. The moot meets less often than it used to.

focuses.name: Crown of the Highlands
focuses.desc: The crown is brought out of its chest and set on a stone above the lake, where every chief can see it. Ostoroth is one kingdom from the first pass to the last pasture.

focuses.name: The Lake Road
focuses.desc: The caravans from Furvior climb the Lake Road past Mora's wharves and into the high pastures. Ostoroth levels the ruts, builds the bridges and sets a toll-house at each crossing.

focuses.name: Friends at Furvior
focuses.desc: Furvior's riders have been friends of the highland markets for generations, and their coin is welcome. A resident factor is sent to the capital with gifts and good wishes.

focuses.name: The Road Is Ours
focuses.desc: The Lake Road is a highland road, and the king says so in every court. Toll-houses are manned by Ostoroth's own wardens, and the charter is free.

focuses.name: Markets of Ostoroth
focuses.desc: Wool, hides and mountain cheese are sold at the capital's covered market. Merchants from the lowlands come for the quality and stay for the brew.

focuses.name: Mora, Our Neighbour
focuses.desc: The lake towns of Mora lie at the foot of the Lake Road, and their boat-guilds are the highlands' only way to the water. A friendly letter costs a rider and a week.

focuses.name: The High Road Grows Rich
focuses.desc: Wagons come and go from dawn to dusk, and the toll-books are thick. The king's treasurers build a second storehouse and then a third.

focuses.name: Highland Companies
focuses.desc: Each clan raises a company of long-spear men, drilled at the autumn gathering. They are lean, silent and hard to move from a ridge.

focuses.name: Crag Forts
focuses.desc: Hill-forts are raised on the crags above the passes, built of dry stone and mortared only at the corners. Each holds a hundred spears and a stock of boulders.

focuses.name: Highland Archers
focuses.desc: Archers shoot from the slopes at moving targets on the valley floor, and the best are given a bow of yew. The old men of the clans still prefer a sling.

focuses.name: Hill Ponies
focuses.desc: Small, shaggy and tireless, the hill ponies climb tracks no lowland horse would try. Ostoroth's riders go where wheels cannot.

focuses.name: The Passes Held
focuses.desc: The king orders the passes held against any host, with signal-horns on every ridge and a company at every gate. The Lake Road can be shut in a morning.

focuses.name: Masters of the Heights
focuses.desc: Captains drill on the high slopes in all weathers, and young chiefs learn to command ridge, ford and pass. The highlands have never lacked brave men; they now have trained ones.

focuses.name: Herds of the High Pastures
focuses.desc: Flocks and herds are counted in the king's book at the spring gathering, and the herd-wardens carry the tally from valley to valley. A kingdom of grass is rarely hungry.

focuses.name: Wool and Hides
focuses.desc: Fulling-mills beside the fast streams and tanning-yards downwind of the towns turn wool and hides into goods worth carrying. The smell is the price of prosperity.

focuses.name: Lake Fisheries
focuses.desc: The upland lakes teem with fish, and the highland fishers sell salted catch to the towns below. Long nets and clinker boats replace the old spear and hide-boat.

focuses.name: Mines of the Crags
focuses.desc: Iron and a little copper lie close to the surface in the crags, and the miners follow the seams by lamplight. The king's smiths are glad of it.

focuses.name: The Highland Granaries
focuses.desc: Oat, barley and dried fish are stored in stone barns in every valley, and the chiefs are told to keep a winter's worth in reserve. A hard winter no longer thins the clans.
